subject.title: Feature request: first-class Telegram reaction triggers for agent wake-up and execution

question: Should OpenClaw adopt the shared `notificationWake.reactions` policy, a Telegram-specific reaction semantics mapping, or a narrower per-message/action design for Telegram reaction-triggered execution?
rationale: The request adds public wake/config semantics for operator control, and the open candidates implement competing API shapes that automation should not choose without maintainer intent.

options.title: Adopt Shared Notification Wake
options.body: Use the queue/wake/off policy from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/83611 as the canonical default-safe contract, then repair or replace it with live Telegram proof.

options.title: Adopt Telegram Semantics Mapping
options.body: Use a Telegram-specific semantics map only if maintainers want per-emoji meanings in the channel config before a cross-channel policy exists.

options.title: Defer Reaction Execution
options.body: Keep reactions passive for now and pause or close implementation candidates until the operator-control product surface is clearer.

recommendation.title: Adopt Shared Notification Wake
recommendation.body: Use the queue/wake/off policy from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/83611 as the canonical default-safe contract, then repair or replace it with live Telegram proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This person owns the open shared-policy candidate and has recent history in the affected Telegram reaction/config path.
